{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I trusted my business partner with the formula for our signature sauce—a family recipe passed down three generations. When our partnership dissolved, he opened a competing restaurant using that exact recipe. He called it his 'own creation.' My grandmother's secret is now his signature dish.

CANDIDATE A:
My dissertation advisor asked to see my theoretical framework 'to offer feedback.' His new book, published six months later, used my central argument without citation. When I raised it, he said ideas discussed in advising belong to the academic community.

CANDIDATE B:
I trusted my business partner with the formula for our signature sauce—a family recipe. When we dissolved the partnership, she returned all documentation and agreed in writing never to use it. She started a new restaurant with completely different cuisine. The trust I placed was respected.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:42"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a betrayal of trust where one party uses the other's intellectual property for personal gain, leading to a conflict over ownership and ethics."}
